title: Customer actionflow: incident choices onepager
content:
Purpose:
This one-pager is a concise, customer-facing artifact combining: (A) a short status-page update template you can paste to status.redwood.ai, and (B) a plain-English post-incident summary + action flow customers can use to choose remediation/replay options and verify outcomes.

High-level TL;DR (status page snippet) - copy/paste friendly:
[Incident title] Intermittent inference integrity and elevated latency (region: us-west-2) — Service degraded — mitigation underway.
Impact: Some requests returned duplicate or truncated outputs and elevated tail latency between 2026-05-05T16:12:00Z and 2026-05-05T18:03:00Z.
What we’re doing: We routed traffic to a compatible model variant and performed a rolling restart of the affected inference pool. A full verification and replay plan is available below.
ETA for full recovery: verification in progress; expected completion 2026-05-07 02:00 UTC.

Customer-facing postmortem summary (short):
- What happened: A small subset of inference requests experienced inconsistent outputs (duplicates/truncation) while overall throughput dropped due to a sizing/regenerator interaction in our autoscaler. This caused retry storms and KV-cache mismatches for tenants using long-context streaming.
- Scope: ~0.8% of requests in us-west-2 during the window; impacts most visible to customers using streaming completions or long-context chat sessions. No data exfiltration suspected.
- Root cause (brief): A metric aggregation bug in the autoscaler incorrectly inferred idle GPU slots during sustained backpressure. The autoscaler triggered accelerated regenerator cycles that evicted stale KV cache entries while sessions were active, producing truncated or repeated token emission in some sessions.

Timeline (concise):
- 2026-05-05 16:12 UTC — Monitoring alert: elevated token-error rate and two downstream SLO alarms.
- 16:20 — Triage started; mitigation plan drafted.
- 16:35 — Temporary routing rule applied: route new streaming sessions to fallback pool with validated cache semantics.
- 16:42 — Autoscaler config change rolled back for affected pool.
- 17:05 — Rolling restart of regenerator hosts started; instance warmup monitored.
- 17:58 — Error rate decreased below threshold; early verification shows majority of in-flight sessions resumed normal output.
- 18:03 — Incident declared mitigated; verification tasks continued overnight.

Actions we took (what we did):
1) Immediate routing: diverted new sessions away from the affected pool to avoid further cache invalidation.
2) Autoscaler hotfix: rolled back the changes that triggered aggressive regeneration and updated guardrails.
3) Service restart: performed a controlled rolling restart of regenerator instances and validated per-session KV-corruption checks.
4) Verification: ran deterministic prompt sets and customer-provided test prompts to validate outputs and latency distributions.
5) Longer-term fixes: implemented a safe-regeneration mode, added a per-tenant cooldown, and scheduled an audit of autoscaler aggregation logic.

Customer choices and recommended action flow (decision steps):
Step 0 - If you see no impact in your tenant: no action required. We’ll notify when verification completes.
Step 1 - If you saw truncated or duplicated outputs and want us to re-run affected requests: opt into the replay program (see opt-in text below). We will only replay requests you explicitly authorize.
Step 2 - If you prefer a self-serve approach: run the provided validation prompts in a staging copy (example below) and confirm outputs to your SRE/CS contact.
Step 3 - If you have compliance/legal questions about replaying tenant data: contact your Redwood account team; we will walk through redaction, consent options, and opt-in consent logs.

Replay opt-in (sample customer-facing consent snippet your legal teams can use):
"I authorize Redwood Inference to reprocess my tenant's specified request IDs and inputs from 2026-05-05 16:00–18:10 UTC for the sole purpose of verifying output integrity and rebuilding derived artifacts. I consent to temporary access by Redwood SREs for debugging; replayed responses will be deleted after verification unless I request retention."
To opt in: reply to this email thread or open incidence JIRA JIRA-INC-3245 with label "replay-opt" and attach a list of request IDs.

Self-checks customers can run (quick):
- If you use streaming: open a new session using the same model and prompt and confirm token-by-token progression; if truncation occurs consistently, capture the session id and send to CS.
- If you use batch/generate: pick 20 sample prompts from the affected window and re-run against the fallback model we routed to (model id: redwood-compat-x1). Compare token counts and end-of-sequence markers.
- Check logs for duplicate response ids (response_id collisions within 10s of each other are a strong signal).

Evidence package we’ll provide to customers who opt in:
- Chronology with timestamps and affected request ids (redacted on request).
- MD5 hashes of inputs and outputs before and after replay.
- A short verification report stating whether the replay changed outputs and our recommended remediation.

Compensation and credits policy (proposal language):
We recognize interruptions cause operational burden. For tenants materially impacted (>=1% of monthly requests affected during the event window), we propose a one-time service credit equal to 5% of the monthly bill for the service month in which the incident occurred, or targeted engineering credits (e.g., professional services time) to assist with replays and verification. Final credit decisions will be handled by CS in coordination with finance based on replay opt-in and verified impact.

Frequently asked Q&A (short):
Q: Was customer data exposed?
A: No evidence of data exfiltration. Replay uses internal logs and stored inputs; we will only replay with explicit customer opt-in.

Q: Will this happen again?
A: We implemented a mitigation and are shipping a fix to the autoscaler metric aggregation. We also added an internal runbook step to pause regeneration during backpressure events.

Q: How do I get help now?
A: Open a support ticket with the label "incident-3245" or email your account team. We will prioritize replays and verification for opted-in customers.

Operational notes for CS/ENG handoff (internal bullets):
- Provide customers the replay opt-in template and a single point of contact (SRE + CS lead).
- For each opted-in tenant: collect request IDs, approximate affected time, and expected verification window.
- Prioritize customers with high-throughput or compliance needs for expedited replay.

Suggested status page timeline entries: (for teams copying into status.redwood.ai)
1) Investigating — time window + short symptom line.
2) Identified & Mitigating — what we changed (routing + rollback).
3) Monitoring — verification underway; expected completion.
4) Resolved — summary + link to postmortem and replay opt-in form.

Draft email subject lines (pick one):
- "Update: Redwood service event — us-west-2 inference integrity (replay option)"
- "Action required: Replay opt-in available for affected requests (Redwood)"

Internal references / next steps:
- Follow up CR to autoscaler metrics, assign to eng-infra (PREQ-221).
- Postmortem doc to be posted in Confluence and linked from customer-facing update.
- CS to prepare list of tenants impacted and outreach schedule (EOD 2026-05-07).

Contact (CS lead):
Maya Chen — maya@redwood.ai — +1 (415) 555-0142

Notes / open questions (working draft):
- Confirm whether we should auto-offer credits or require customer request. Recommend CS-run review before public credit offers.
- Determine retention policy for replayed outputs (default: delete after verification unless customer requests otherwise).

----
Version history: v0.1 initial draft 2026-05-06 by Maya Chen; v0.2 minor edits 2026-05-07 (added compensation proposal and opt-in wording).
